Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll inspect the workspace instructions and inherited rollout evidence first. I’ll also apply the required fish-control bookshelf protocol and the wake-visual inspection skill before proposing or editing the single candidate.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis, a durable guidance change, and a final contract check; CFD itself is explicitly out of scope. I’m now reading the inherited guidance and both applicable skill protocols, then I’ll inspect every sampled rollout’s metrics and keyframes.

All four sampled policies capture from direct-uniform still water. The useful contrast is finer: three proximity-preview variants finish near `22.187T`, while the fixed-lead comparison finishes at `22.308T`; I’m checking whether that numerical advantage corresponds to the same self-propelled route and wake rather than a rendering or trajectory artifact.

The inherited logs add two decisive controls: slow-route proximity preview is the only new positive result (`22.1595T`, mean distance `2.105808L`), while allowing proximity preview only to reduce the rudder collapses exactly to the slower fixed-lead trajectory. I’m consulting the bookshelf references now; any transfer will be limited to one bounded state-feedback invariant, not a gain copy.

The selected candidate uses the sampled best policy as its base and adds one bounded architecture change: the same proximity-conditioned, de-yawed target-line preview that improved slow anterior curvature will also advance the existing anterior redirect gate, without changing its acceleration ceiling or any carrier/posterior authority. This follows the bookshelf’s sensor-triggered redirect invariant while preserving the traveling bend.

The candidate file now contains one policy only, with every active parameter still owned by `target_policy_params()`. I’m updating the reusable experience bank with both the new positive boundary (slow anterior preview) and the matched negative boundary (rudder-release-only prediction), without treating this unevaluated candidate as evidence.

The self-review shows the solver differs from the sampled best only in the intended redirect-gate timing, and the new parameter is present in the returned schema. I’m now invoking the required check-runner to validate the guidance delta, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary rules without CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account. I’m using a standard verification agent as a fallback to execute the exact three commands from that configuration; the checks and no-CFD constraint remain unchanged.

The policy and boundary checks pass. The guidance check found a duplicated “copied to guidance” marker for the same optimizer in the rendered README, unrelated to the content changes. I’m correcting only that duplicate assignment marker, then rerunning the failed check as required.

Completed exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:118) adds proximity-previewed anterior redirect gating.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:281) adds the evidence-backed anterior-preview lesson and rudder-release negative result.

All configured checks pass: guidance delta, finite two-joint Julia contract, and editable boundary. No CFD was run.
